Fit an ordinary least-squares model bundle

Source: R/lm-fit.R
fit_linear.Rd

Fits stats::lm() to one dataset, or once per imputation of stacked long-form data, and combines imputations with Rubin's rules. A single fit is inferred on the t distribution with its residual degrees of freedom, as PROC REG reports it.

Usage

fit_linear(
  formula,
  data,
  outcome_col = NULL,
  id_col = "id",
  imputation_col = NULL,
  prediction_col = "fitted"
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula. The response may be transformed, e.g. log(los) ~ age. A . on the right-hand side expands to the data's other columns, excluding the response, id_col and imputation_col.

data

A data frame, or stacked imputations when imputation_col is set.

outcome_col

Outcome column. By default the one variable in the formula's response; if supplied, it must be one of the variables in the response.

id_col

Patient identifier column. Required only when imputation_col is set.

imputation_col

Imputation-index column, or NULL for one dataset.

prediction_col

Name of the fitted-value column added to $data, averaged across imputations.

Value

An object of class c("rm_fit", "ps_data"). $tables$fit_quality gives each fit's residual degrees of freedom, residual standard error and R-squared; R-squared is NA for imputed data, where Rubin's rules define none.

See also

fit_logistic(), bs_continuous()

Examples

dta <- sample_ps_data(n = 150, seed = 42)
fit <- fit_linear(ef ~ age + female, data = dta)
fit$tables$estimates[, c("term", "estimate", "std.error", "p.value")]
#>          term   estimate  std.error      p.value
#> 1 (Intercept) 68.7280984 5.12425021 2.156296e-32
#> 2         age -0.1867446 0.06779147 6.237331e-03
#> 3      female  0.1259720 1.20495525 9.168075e-01
